profiles.name: 参考動画2本｜軽量マンガ画風のみ固定 v2
profiles.stylePrompt: Match only the shared production grammar of the benchmark videos: simple flat Japanese YouTube web-manga art at the visual information density of a clean 640x360 frame; mostly uniform thin charcoal-black contours; smooth uncomplicated face shapes; eyes made from a few clean strokes; a minimal single-line nose; a small simple mouth; pale flat skin with at most one restrained cel-shadow shape; hair drawn as a few broad graphic masses with one flat highlight band; clothes as broad flat fills with very few fold lines; light cream, muted blue, sage, dusty pink and brown palette; believable Japanese rooms, offices and streets simplified to visibly lower detail than the characters. Emotion comes from pose, gaze and mouth shape rather than wrinkles, facial planes or muscles. Keep the finish intentionally modest and readable, never realistic, gritty, glossy, cinematic or game-art-like.
profiles.compositionPrompt: Always output one full-bleed 16:9 illustration. Use mostly eye-level normal-lens framing equivalent to 35-70mm: medium two-shots for dialogue, clean reaction close-ups, occasional waist-up three-shots and sparse establishing wides. Place characters on thirds with readable silhouettes and grounded eyelines. Preserve a clean upper or outer negative-space zone opposite the current speaker for the later deterministic vertical speech bubble; never draw the bubble in the image. Do not center every actor symmetrically, use extreme wide-angle distortion, crop faces at the eyes/chin, or hide story-critical hands and props.
profiles.shotRhythmPrompt: For a sequence, target approximately 10% establishing/location shots, 55% medium or two-person dialogue shots, and 35% reaction close-ups. Alternate shot/reverse-shot and reaction framing; never repeat the same camera distance more than twice. Each still carries one clear action, emotion or reveal, with restrained acting except at the scripted climax.
profiles.continuityPrompt: Character identity comes only from approved candidate, turnaround and expression sheets. Every benchmark image is STYLE-ONLY and must never supply a face, hair, age, body, clothing or pose. Keep each approved character's exact face, hair, age, build, clothing and accessories. Keep recurring locations on one stable architecture, furniture plan, palette, time-of-day logic and light direction across all cuts. Props remain the same design and scale between shots.
profiles.outputPrompt: Single 16:9 landscape frame, clean edges, no panel borders, no collage, no split screen, no built-in captions, no speech bubbles, no narration boxes, no readable text, no logos, no watermark. Leave all typography and balloons to BuzzAssist's deterministic overlay stage.
profiles.negativePrompt: realistic facial planes, angular cheekbone modeling, detailed lips, pores, stubble, deep wrinkles, under-eye bags, huge eyebrows, muscular neck, action-hero anatomy, gritty seinen face, yakuza-game rendering, thick aggressive ink, cross-hatching, individual hair strands, realistic fabric texture, glossy cinematic light, gradients, 3D render, photorealism, chibi, western superhero anatomy, neon grading, crushed blacks, orange-teal grade, excessive depth-of-field blur, fisheye, dutch angle without story need, duplicated people, copied benchmark identity, mixed character identities, gibberish text, speech balloons, captions, UI, screenshot artifacts
